answered.sql: SELECT p.name, f.fieldName FROM Physicists p JOIN Physicist_Fields pf ON p.id = pf.physicistId JOIN Fields f ON pf.fieldId = f.id

candidates.meaning: Show the field names for each physicist.
candidates.sql: SELECT P.name, F.fieldName FROM Physicists P JOIN Physicist_Fields PF ON P.id = PF.physicistId JOIN Fields F ON PF.fieldId = F.id

candidates.meaning: Show a list of fields each physicist works in, including duplicates.
candidates.sql: SELECT T3.fieldName FROM Physicists AS T1 JOIN Physicist_Fields AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.physicistId JOIN Fields AS T3 ON T2.fieldId = T3.id

candidates.meaning: List all fields and count how many physicists work in each field, without duplicates.
candidates.sql: SELECT T3.fieldName, COUNT(*) FROM Physicists AS T1 JOIN Physicist_Fields AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.physicistId JOIN Fields AS T3 ON T2.fieldId = T3.id GROUP BY T3.fieldName

candidates.meaning: Show a list of unique fields each physicist works in, without duplicates for each physicist.
candidates.sql: SELECT T1.name, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT T3.fieldName) FROM Physicists AS T1 JOIN Physicist_Fields AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.physicistId JOIN Fields AS T3 ON T2.fieldId = T3.id GROUP BY T1.id
